## Summary

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Projects | 5 (3 src + 2 test) |
| Directory.Build.props | ❌ Missing |
| Directory.Build.targets | ❌ Missing |
| Central Package Management | ❌ Not adopted |

---

## 🔴 Errors (Likely Broken or Will Cause Issues)

### 1. Package version inconsistency — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |
|---------|---------|
| Core | 8.0.0 |
| Api | 8.0.0 |
| Services | **8.0.1** |

This means the resolved version depends on NuGet's version unification at restore time. While NuGet picks the highest, this creates confusion and makes it easy to accidentally regress. With transitive references, `Api` → `Services` → `8.0.1` means the API project will silently use 8.0.1 anyway, making its explicit `8.0.0` reference misleading.

### 2. Test package version inconsistency

| Package | Core.Tests | Api.Tests |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk | 17.10.0 | **17.9.0** |
| xunit | 2.8.1 | **2.7.1** |
| xunit.runner.visualstudio | 2.8.1 | **2.5.6** |

These version mismatches mean the two test projects run on different test infrastructure. This can cause subtle differences in test behavior and makes upgrades error-prone.

---

## 🟡 Warnings (Anti-Patterns)

### 3. Massive property duplication across all projects

These 7 properties are copy-pasted identically in all 5 projects:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

**Impact**: Every new project must remember to add all of these. If a policy changes (e.g., TFM upgrade to net9.0), you must update 5 files instead of 1.

### 4. Duplicated `PrintBuildInfo` target in 3 source projects

The same custom target is repeated verbatim in Core, Api, and Services. This violates DRY and belongs in `Directory.Build.targets`.

### 5. Duplicated `DocumentationFile` property in 3 source projects

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

Same pattern — should be centralized.

### 6. `PrintBuildInfo` target has no `Inputs`/`Outputs`

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
```

Without `Inputs`/`Outputs`, this target always executes even on no-op builds. For a `<Message>` task this is harmless (it's cheap), so this is a minor warning — but it sets a bad precedent for future custom targets.

### 7. Scattered package versions without Central Package Management

With 5 projects and growing, managing versions per-project is error-prone (as demonstrated by the inconsistencies above).

### 8. Multiple `<PropertyGroup>` elements in source projects

`DocumentationFile` sits in its own `<PropertyGroup>` separated from the main one. While valid, it reduces readability and suggests organic growth without cleanup.

---

## 🔵 Suggestions

### 9. `System.Text.Json` 8.0.5 in Core is transitively available to Api

`Api` explicitly references `System.Text.Json 8.0.5` AND references `Core` which also has it. The explicit reference in `Api` is redundant unless you specifically need to pin the version there. With CPM, this becomes moot.

### 10. Mixed JSON libraries — `System.Text.Json` and `Newtonsoft.Json`

`Services` uses `Newtonsoft.Json` while `Core` and `Api` use `System.Text.Json`. This isn't an MSBuild issue per se, but it's worth noting as a potential architectural inconsistency.

### 11. Test projects missing `coverlet.collector` for code coverage

Standard .NET test templates include `coverlet.collector`. Its absence means `dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"` won't work without additional setup.

---

## 🟢 Positive Practices

- ✅ SDK-style projects throughout (no legacy format)
- ✅ `TreatWarningsAsErrors` enabled everywhere — good quality gate
- ✅ `Nullable` enabled — modern C# safety
- ✅ `IsPackable=false` on test projects — prevents accidental NuGet publishing
- ✅ `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` — consistent code style enforcement
- ✅ Clean project references with relative paths

---

## Concrete Recommendations & File Contents

### 1. Create `Directory.Build.props` (repo root)

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>

  <!-- XML documentation for non-test source projects -->

    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Test project defaults -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
    <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>

### 1. Package version inconsistency — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |

| Core | 8.0.0 |
| Api | 8.0.0 |
| Services | **8.0.1** |

This means the resolved version depends on NuGet's version unification at restore time. While NuGet picks the highest, this creates confusion and makes it easy to accidentally regress. ### 3. Massive property duplication across all projects

`DocumentationFile` sits in its own `<PropertyGroup>` separated from the main one. While valid, it reduces readability and suggests organic growth without cleanup.
